hook: Broader Spike-recognizing T cell receptor repertoires predicted fewer symptomatic COVID cases after a booster

readout.label: Hazard ratio, symptomatic infection, higher breadth

summary: Using participants' HLA types and T cell receptor sequences from a third-dose vaccine trial, the team estimated how many Spike fragments each person's T cells could recognize. Higher breadth went with lower risk of symptomatic infection, even after accounting for antibodies and interferon-gamma responses. It is an observational association in one trial, so it does not show that breadth causes protection.
title: Personalized HLA-aware TCR measure predicts the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection following booster vaccination
